title.title: Classwise permanence for weakly reversible mass-action systems
title.subtitle: Claim: in every weakly reversible mass-action network, species stay bounded and away from zero, uniformly

beats.text: Weakly reversible: every reaction can be undone by a chain of reactions
Claim: each conservation class $P$ has one compact convex set $K_P$
Every trajectory enters it in finite time (schematic)

achievement.label: Persistence and permanence conjectures, weakly reversible networks
statement: \text{entered by every trajectory in finite time}
achievement.context: Before: two species (2013), one linkage class (2014, 2020); the general case open

verify.detail: Lean covers boundedness and persistence with start-dependent bounds, not uniform permanence
verify.ourCheck: We read the abstracts and main statements; we did not build the Lean

sources.quote: Craciun, Nazarov & Pantea (SIAM J. Appl. Math. 2013): permanence for two-species (endotactic) systems

Gopalkrishnan, Miller & Shiu (SIAM J. Appl. Dyn. Syst. 2014): permanence for strongly endotactic networks, incl. one linkage class; Boros & Hofbauer (SIAM J. Appl. Dyn. Syst. 2020): another single-linkage-class proof
Lean (MassAction challenge, docs/149.md) covers the boundedness/persistence statement with initial-state-dependent bounds, not the classwise uniform permanence
each of whom read the catalogue summary, every abstract, and the introduction and main theorem statements of every principal manuscript in their group
I did not build the Lean library, run Comparator or execute any code from the release.

plain: In a chemical soup where every reaction can be undone, no ingredient runs out or piles up without limit

voice.text: If every reaction can be undone, no species dies out or explodes.
Every path enters one safe region.
Claimed: both conjectures proved, for fixed rate constants.
Lean covers only part of it.
